approach: Change the `push:` entry under `on:` in .github/workflows/ci.yml from "every branch" to `branches: [main]`, leaving pull_request, workflow_dispatch and the weekly schedule as they are, and add a short comment above it saying why. Append decision D125 to the end of docs/decisions.md (after D124), in the same layout as D124, with the alternatives and the PR #185 timings labeled as taken from the request. Add one bullet under the existing `### Changed` section of [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md. No job names, cache keys, pass-marker logic or other workflows change. The header comment (lines 1-11) still holds: it says only a default-branch push saves the shared caches, and that pass markers are saved on pull-request branches, both of which remain true, so it is not edited. The post-landing outcome is recorded in D125 as a follow-up and not claimed.

decisions.reason: Main pushes still run after each landing and save the shared default-branch caches (header comment, lines 5-7). Pull-request branches then get only the pull_request run, in the pull request's own cache scope, which the required check reads.

rejected.why: Nothing would run on main after a merge, so the shared default-branch caches would refresh only on the weekly schedule.
Any new branch name would still run twice, so the rule is weaker than an allow-list.

rejected.option: Keep `push:` on all branches and add a `concurrency` group with cancel-in-progress.
rejected.why: Push runs would still start and use runners, and they would still sit in the push cache scope that misses the cached pass.

rejected.option: A `paths` filter on the push trigger.
rejected.why: It does not remove the duplicate for code changes, which is the case in the request.

decisions.choice: Append D125 at the end of docs/decisions.md and change no earlier entry.
decisions.reason: The D122 test pins SHA-256 hashes of the log through D121, so only appending passes. Appending needs no change to docs/decision-links.toml (D122 notes this).

rejected.option: Edit an existing decision or insert in the middle of the log.
rejected.why: The pinned hash test fails on any edit before the end.

files.purpose: Change the push trigger to `branches: [main]` and add a comment giving the reason (cache scope, PR #185 timings, D125). Nothing else changes.
Append D125 after D124: the case, the decision, rejected alternatives, tradeoff, reversal cost, provenance, and the post-landing follow-up. Append only.
Add one bullet under [Unreleased] ### Changed describing the push trigger limit and pointing to D125.

steps: Read crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs around `early_run_wait` to see whether it filters by event. If it needs a push run, stop and report.

Edit .github/workflows/ci.yml: under `on:`, add a comment above `push:` (cache scope, PR #185 timings, D125), then change `push:` to `push:` with `branches: [main]`. Leave the header comment, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, schedule and job names unchanged.
Append the D125 entry to the end of docs/decisions.md, using the D124 layout. Include the rejected alternatives, the PR #185 timings labeled as stated in the request, and the post-landing follow-up.
Add one bullet under `### Changed` in [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md, after the D124 bullet, pointing to D125.
Run `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy`; both must pass.
Check the diff: only the three named files changed, and the job name is unchanged.

risks.risk: Pushes to branches other than main no longer run CI, including athena/records.
risks.mitigation: Code changes are covered by the pull_request run; workflow_dispatch still runs on demand. D125 records the change.

risks.risk: The early_run_wait logic may count or wait for push runs that no longer exist.
risks.mitigation: Read gh.rs before editing; if it depends on a push run, stop and report instead of changing Rust code.

risks.risk: The one-run-per-commit outcome is not verified before landing.
risks.mitigation: D125 records it as a follow-up to check on the next landing's pull request. The decision does not claim it.

risks.risk: Editing an earlier decision entry or the middle of docs/decisions.md breaks the D122 pinned hash test.
risks.mitigation: Append D125 only, at the end of the file.

demonstrations.method: Read the on: block of the changed workflow and its diff.
demonstrations.observes: The push entry has only `branches: [main]`; the pull_request, workflow_dispatch and cron lines are unchanged; a comment above the push entry states the cache-scope reason and cites D125 and PR #185.

A new `## D125` entry follows D124 with Case, Decision, Alternatives (the rejected options above), Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. It gives the PR #185 timings (pull_request run 26 s via cached pass, two push runs about 16 min, landing waited 17m51s) and labels them as stated in the request. Earlier lines are unchanged.
One new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` in `### Changed`, after the D124 bullet, describing the push trigger limit to main and pointing to D125.

demonstrations.method: Confirm the change set and that the job name line is untouched.
demonstrations.observes: Only .github/workflows/ci.yml, docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md appear. In the ci.yml diff, `name: fmt, clippy, tests` and the job structure are unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Read the header comment (lines 1-11) to confirm it is unchanged and still accurate for the new trigger.
demonstrations.observes: Lines 1-11 do not appear in the diff. The text still says only a default-branch push saves shared caches and that pass markers are saved on pull-request branches, which remains true with the new trigger.

demonstrations.method: Run the Rust test and lint commands.
demonstrations.observes: Both finish with exit status 0 and no warnings. The policy tests that read ci.yml (xtask/tests/policy.rs, checks_job_steps) and the D122 log-hash test still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A broken YAML edit, a changed job name, or an edit to an earlier decision entry would fail cargo test; a clippy warning would fail cargo clippy.

demonstrations.method: Cannot be run before landing. The producer and verifier cannot observe the next landing's pull request. It is recorded in D125 as a follow-up.
demonstrations.observes: After landing: the next landing's pull request shows one CI run per commit. Until then the claim is not made.

open_questions: Does `early_run_wait` in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs filter runs by event? It was not read. If it expects a push run, the wait for the early commit's run could change. The producer should read it before editing ci.yml; this plan changes no Rust code.
The request assumes the host's default branch is named `main`. The plan relies on that and did not check it against the host settings.
Pushes to non-main branches (such as the `athena/records` branch) will no longer start CI. This is intended, since records are not code, but the decision entry should say so.
